\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Choice Replay: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.ChoiceReplay}.

\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Choice Replay: Results}

\begin{definition}[Nondeterministic machine replay]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.replayTM}
\label{Turing.NDTM.replayTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.NDTM}
Given a nondeterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and state set
$S$, construct a deterministic machine with $k+1$ work tapes and the same initial state.
At each step, it reads the last work tape's scanned Boolean value as the choice bit,
treating a blank as false, and uses that choice to select the original machine's
transition; the original $k$ work-tape actions, input movement, output, and successor
state are retained, while the added tape is left unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Adding a choice tape]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.withChoiceTape}
\label{Turing.NDTM.withChoiceTape}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
Given a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes on a Boolean input, a tape
content function from the integers to optional Boolean values, and an integer head
position, form a configuration with $k+1$ work tapes by appending that tape and head
position as the last work tape. The state, input-head position, and output are
unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Replaying a choice word]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.replayTM_runFrom}
\label{Turing.NDTM.replayTM_runFrom}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.replayTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt, Turing.NDTM.stepWith, Turing.NDTM.withChoiceTape}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean alphabet and state
set $S$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $N$ on $x$.
Given a Boolean word $s$ and a natural number $t\le |s|$, there is a position $p\le t$
such that, if the run of $N$ from $c$ under the first $t$ bits of $s$ has not halted,
then $p=t$; and after $t$ steps the replay machine for $N$, started from $c$ with a
choice tape containing $s$ and its head at position zero, has the same configuration as
the run of $N$ under those first $t$ bits, with the choice tape unchanged and its head
at position $p$.
\end{theorem}
